brief: Service benchmark: Dubai ranked first among cities in the UN's Local Online Service Index 2026 with a score of 100%, up from joint fourth in 2024, in a survey themed 'From Digital Government to Agentic Government' (Dubai Media Office, 19 Nov).

Agent-led payments: Visa has opened Agentic Ready to merchants, acquirers and payment providers with more than 140 participants (Visa, 17 Nov), and Salesforce's own forecast expects AI and agents to influence 21% of global Cyber Week online sales, or $75.8bn (Salesforce, 19 Nov).

Türkiye: CarrefourSA opened its 56th Gurme store at City's İstanbul AVM in Kozyatağı (Habertürk and Karar, 19 Nov), Kanyon is bringing back Radyo Kanyon with studios inside the mall, and Esas Gayrimenkul set out the non-rent income lines at its malls (Mall Report, 19 Nov).

Brands: Dunkin' opened its first restaurant in Kazakhstan, in Almaty (Kursiv, 13 Nov), and Chalhoub Group plans 2027 GCC stores for Gap, Banana Republic and Athleta as Athleta prepares its UAE debut (Gulf Business, 5 Nov; The National, 12 Nov).

Directory checks: Souq Sharq in Kuwait City was emptied by 31 Jan 2026 for a refurbishment PPP won by United Real Estate Company, The Avenues - Bahrain's western expansion opened in Q2 2025, and Majid Al Futtaim gives City Centre Bahrain 153k m2 and Mall of Egypt 170k m2 of GLA.
weekly_brief: Week 47 (16 to 20 November): 46 findings and 12 library documents across five editions, with Friday's checks of directory listings.
Kuwait: Mabanee's Aventura Mall opened to visitors on 15 Nov with 15 Alshaya stores, among them H&M, Boots and Shake Shack, and Mabanee confirmed that The Avenues Riyadh opens on 27 March 2027.

Saudi Arabia: the Cabinet approved a unified Consumer Protection Law with fines of up to SAR 8 million; Knowledge Economic City's shareholders approved renaming it Al-Jiwar Economic City, and it expects two Madinah shopping centres to start trading in 2027; Al Othaim Markets lost SAR 39.26m in Q3 after problems with an ERP rollout.

UAE: Majid Al Futtaim will build an AED 260m staff parking facility to free more than 1,000 shopper spaces at Mall of the Emirates by December 2027; Alef Group's 06 Mall will carry a façade screen from CITIX MENA; Spinneys expects its first stores in Kuwait and the Philippines in Q1 2027; and talabat raised its 2026 guidance again.

Egypt, Türkiye, Iraq and Kazakhstan: Lulu opened a hypermarket in Obour City; Civilia launched STEEP Mall in Sheikh Zayed City; ZEISS opened at İstanbul AVM and KİP opened its first Iraq store at Grand Majidi Mall in Erbil; CarrefourSA opened its 56th Gurme store; Kanyon revived Radyo Kanyon; and Dunkin' opened its first Kazakhstan restaurant in Almaty.

Service and AI: Dubai ranked first in the UN's Local Online Service Index 2026 and approved a City AI Agent, and Dubai Municipality unveiled D.Mind; the EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act would give consumers a right to human customer service; and Visa opened Agentic Ready to merchants after OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet let its agents pay for purchases.

Directory checks: Souq Sharq in Kuwait City was emptied for a refurbishment PPP won by United Real Estate Company, The Avenues - Bahrain's western expansion opened in Q2 2025, Majid Al Futtaim gives City Centre Bahrain 153k m2 and Mall of Egypt 170k m2 of GLA, and the directory's 'D2 Community Centre' is DAMAC Hills 2 Community Centre.

findings.title: Dubai ranks first among cities in the UN's Local Online Service Index 2026, with a score of 100%
findings.summary: Dubai ranked first globally in the Local Online Service Index (LOSI) 2026, part of the 2026 UN E-Government Survey by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, with a perfect score of 100%, Dubai Media Office reported on 19 Nov. The city has risen from 16th in 2018 and 2020 to fifth in 2022, joint fourth in 2024 and first in 2026; the index rates city-level online services on 101 indicators across six criteria. The survey's theme is 'From Digital Government to Agentic Government', and Hamad Obaid Al Mansoori, Director General of Digital Dubai, is quoted; the release does not say how many cities were assessed.
findings.why: The UN's benchmark for city-level online services sets the standard that Dubai residents now hold every service provider to, malls, retailers and banks included, and its theme points to AI agents as the next phase of service.

findings.title: CarrefourSA opens its 56th Gurme store, at City's İstanbul AVM in Kozyatağı, Istanbul
findings.summary: CarrefourSA has opened its 56th store in its gastronomy-led Gurme format, at City's İstanbul AVM in the Kozyatağı district of Istanbul, Habertürk and Karar reported on 19 Nov in items that read as a company announcement. The store has fish, butcher, fruit and vegetable, delicatessen and bakery counters, with organic, vegan, shellfish and imported ranges; neither report gives its size or opening day. Chief executive Hatice Evren said food retail is changing with lifestyles and customer expectations.
findings.why: A gastronomy-led grocery format taking space in an Istanbul mall, and a store-count milestone for one of Türkiye's main grocers.

findings.title: Kanyon brings back Radyo Kanyon in its 20th year, with Radyo Fenomen studios inside the mall
findings.summary: Kanyon in Istanbul is reviving Radyo Kanyon, the radio venture it started with, in its 20th year through a partnership with Radyo Fenomen, Mall Report reported on 19 Nov. New broadcast studios inside the mall, which visitors can experience on site, carry Radyo Fenomen, FenomenTürk, İstanbul FM and Radyo Boombox. Kanyon Yönetim general manager İrem Yücel Kaymak and Bayrakstar Medya deputy general manager Uyum Varol Kebabcı are quoted; no start date, studio size or location in the mall is given.
findings.why: A mall turning live media production into a visitor attraction, a format that members weighing entertainment and media uses can study.

findings.title: Esas Gayrimenkul widens non-rent income at its Turkish malls, from media and pop-ups to parking, EV charging and solar
findings.summary: Nezaket Akçakaya, senior director of property management at Esas Gayrimenkul, told Mall Report (19 Nov) that its shopping centres earn non-rent income from common-area leasing, advertising and digital screens, events and sponsorship, kiosks, pop-ups and seasonal sales points, parking, EV charging and solar installations, with parking and EV charging run on space-leasing and revenue-share models. The company builds brand partnerships across its malls in several cities and is developing a private hygiene area at its Çanakkale mall as a new service and revenue line. For 2027 it says the aim is not a higher non-rent share of income but sustainable models that improve the visitor experience and long-term asset value; the share and growth figures in the interview are not repeated here, as no second source gives them.
findings.why: Income from media, parking, EV charging and solar is a live topic for GCC mall owners, and the interview sets out how one Turkish manager runs these lines.

findings.title: Salesforce forecasts that AI and agents will influence $75.8bn, or 21%, of global Cyber Week online sales (vendor forecast)
findings.summary: Salesforce's own forecast, drawn from its Shopping Index of more than 1.5 billion shoppers, expects global online sales of $357bn in Cyber Week (24 to 30 Nov 2026), up 6% year on year, with $75.8bn, or 21%, influenced by AI and agents, against $67bn in 2025. It expects AI-driven traffic to rise 104% year on year and 20% of holiday shopping traffic to be nonhuman, and says shoppers referred by AI are twice as likely to convert. The Middle East and Africa is one of the index's 18 markets, but the forecast gives no regional figures.
findings.why: Gulf retailers run their own late-November sales and the Dubai Shopping Festival opens on 4 Dec, so the share of traffic arriving through AI assistants and agents bears on how they measure and serve online demand.

findings.title: Visa opens Agentic Ready to merchants, acquirers and payment providers, starting with more than 140 participants
findings.summary: Visa has extended Agentic Ready, part of Visa Intelligent Commerce, from card issuers to the acceptance side, so that merchants, payment service providers, acquirers and commerce platforms can prepare for purchases started by AI agents (release dated 17 Nov). The programme launches there with more than 140 participants, among them Adyen, Checkout.com, Stripe, PayPal, Worldline, Fiserv and Ant International, alongside more than 175 issuers across 45 markets, and more are expected to join throughout 2027. Visa's UAE newsroom named nine UAE participants in the issuer phase on 20 May 2026, among them Emirates NBD, Mashreq, ADCB, ADIB, Tabby and Wio; the new release names no Gulf merchant or retailer.
findings.why: It brings a card network's preparation for agent-led payments to the merchant side, the open question on the agent-led shopping watch item, and UAE banks and fintechs are already in the issuer phase.

findings.title: Oman Investment Authority completes seven industrial, energy and water projects worth more than OMR 1.6 billion
findings.summary: Oman Investment Authority (OIA) said on 18 Nov that seven national projects worth more than OMR 1.6 billion are complete and will be inaugurated in stages for Oman's National Day (Oman News Agency, in Times of Oman). The largest are the United Solar Polysilicon plant in Sohar Freezone (OMR 668 million, developed with Future Fund Oman) and OQ Group's Ladayn Polymer Park (approximately OMR 576.5 million); the others are Orion Solar (OMR 177.5 million), the 327 MW Rawafed wind and solar portfolio of OQ Alternative Energy and TotalEnergies Renewables (OMR 109 million) and three Nama Water Services networks in Manah, Bahla and Ibri. None of the projects is a retail or mall scheme.
findings.why: Corporate news from a member: Oman's sovereign fund is bringing large industrial, energy and water investments into operation around National Day.

sources.outlet: Oman News Agency (Times of Oman copy)

findings.title: Dunkin' opens its first restaurant in Kazakhstan, in Almaty, under franchisee SGK Partners
findings.summary: Dunkin' has opened its first restaurant in Kazakhstan, at the corner of Gogol and Kunaev streets in Almaty, with a ceremonial opening on 12 Nov, Kursiv reported on 13 Nov; Forbes Kazakhstan reported the opening the same day. SGK Partners holds an exclusive agreement to develop the brand's restaurants in Kazakhstan, and both outlets name Kusto Group founder Erkin Tatishev as one of the project's participants. The partners intend to expand but gave no number of restaurants, cities or dates, and no mall site is named; Forbes Kazakhstan says Inspire Brands, Dunkin's parent, sees the entry as part of its expansion in Central Asia.
findings.why: A US franchise brand entering Kazakhstan with a local operator that plans to expand is a tenant lead for malls in Almaty and Astana.

findings.title: Athleta prepares its regional debut in the UAE as Chalhoub Group plans 2027 stores for Gap Inc.'s brands
findings.summary: Gap Inc.'s women's activewear brand Athleta is preparing to enter the Middle East, beginning with the UAE, with a campaign, 'My World. My Rules', fronted by Emirati racing driver Amna Al Qubaisi, Egyptian filmmaker Salma Elkashef and Saudi endurance athlete Lojain Alrefae, The National reported on 12 Nov; it gives no launch date, sales channel or store site. In a Gulf Business interview published on 5 Nov, David Vercruysse, president of managed companies at Chalhoub Group, which holds Gap, Banana Republic and Athleta in the GCC under the partnership announced on 4 Aug, said Gap is live online in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait and Banana Republic online in the UAE, with physical stores to follow in 2027; he gave no online launch date for Athleta.
findings.why: Chalhoub's 2027 store rollout for three US fashion brands is a leasing lead for GCC malls.

findings.title: Souq Sharq in Kuwait City has been emptied for a refurbishment PPP won by United Real Estate Company; the directory still lists it as expanding
findings.summary: Wafra Real Estate, which managed Souq Sharq for the state, told all tenants and investors at the waterfront mall to vacate their units by 31 Jan 2026 at the request of the Ministry of Finance; the fish market and yacht marina were not affected (Arab Times, 6 Nov 2025). Kuwait's Authority for Partnership Projects (KAPP) then awarded the rehabilitation, renovation, development, operation and management of phase three of the Sharq waterfront project to United Real Estate Company under a 15-year arrangement (MEED, 26 Feb 2026), and Kuwait Times (6 Aug 2026) ties that award to Souq Sharq's redevelopment. No reopening date or new leasable area has been published by these outlets. The MECSR Directory lists the mall as expanding, with 35,000 sqm of GLA, a 1998 opening and National Real Estate Company as owner.
findings.why: A listed Kuwait City mall is closed for redevelopment under a new operator, so its listing should not print as trading or expanding.

findings.title: The Avenues - Bahrain's western expansion opened in Q2 2025, doubling its leasable area to 84,000 sqm; the directory still lists it as expanding

The MECSR Directory lists the mall as expanding, with the same 84,000 sqm of GLA and a 2017 opening, so only its status needs to change. The page does not name the owning company.
findings.why: Moves a member's listing from expanding to open, with the expansion complete, before the 2027 Directory prints.

No GCC bank, payment network or retailer had set rules to admit or block outside AI shopping agents by 20 Nov. New: Visa has opened Agentic Ready to merchants, acquirers and payment providers with more than 140 participants, after nine UAE banks and fintechs joined its issuer phase in May (Visa, 17 Nov; see 20 Nov). Also: the EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act (11 Nov) would give consumers a right to human customer service, and Sourcing Journal (16 Nov) reports that it would let shoppers who buy through AI agents set and change the agents' key parameters (see 19 Nov). Also: Daydream's stylist agent can complete purchases through one-click checkout, without the report saying how each purchase is approved (TechCrunch, 17 Nov; see 18 Nov). Also: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets its dots agents complete purchases with tokenised cards and Face ID or fingerprint approval for each purchase, first for some US Pro subscribers, and OpenAI published a Commerce Partner Playbook for retailers (TechCrunch, 13 Nov; see 16 Nov). Also: OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT lets companies claim their profiles and add product feeds, with Business Agents first for US online sellers (Reuters, 10 Nov; see 12 Nov). Also: CrediMax and Mastercard will explore agentic commerce for Bahrain merchants, starting with Mastercard's Agent Suite for Merchants (Mastercard, 4 Nov; see 10 Nov), and Zalando launched an agent that buys from other retailers inside its app (Reuters, 3 Nov; see 10 Nov). Earlier context: American Express's Intent Intelligence framework (13 Oct), Meta and Sierra's Personal Agent Protocol (14 Oct), Amazon and eBay blocking agents (16 Oct), Walmart's Agent Gateway (21 Oct), US banks restricting third-party agents (23 Oct), BCG's survey of large retailers (21 Oct, see 28 Oct), PYMNTS and Visa on UAE merchants' readiness (26 Oct), Meta's Muse (28 Oct), Home Depot's rules for agents (29 Oct), Retail Dive's holiday survey round-up (3 Nov), and Amazon's Alexa for Shopping for outside merchants (4 Nov) and text-to-shop test (6 Nov)
watch.source: Visa, 17 Nov 2026; European Commission, 11 Nov 2026; Sourcing Journal, 16 Nov 2026; TechCrunch, 13 and 17 Nov 2026; Reuters, 10 Nov 2026; Mastercard, 4 Nov 2026
